A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same stationary-MMD research and contain readable text, equations, figures and Appendices A–C. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture and House8L/Elevators experiments, including integration errors, MMD comparisons, stationarity verification and a kernel ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds higher-dimensional Gaussian-mixture results and kernel-thinning sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 corrects the gradient direction in the displayed deterministic and noisy updates: v1 Equations (8)–(9) subtract the target-minus-particle gradient difference, whereas v2 Equations (7)–(8) subtract its reverse. This aligns with the existing Appendix B.4.1 construction; the underlying uniformly weighted MMD particle-flow method remains.

E1.justification: v2 adds Gaussian-mixture evaluations in dimensions 10 and 50 (Table 1). The two-dimensional mixture, House8L and Elevators remain, so coverage expands to higher-dimensional synthetic scenarios within the same task family.

E2.justification: QMC participates in the Gaussian-mixture plots in v1 Figure 3 but disappears from the corresponding curves and legend in v2 Figure 2, despite remaining described in the text. IID, kernel herding, kernel thinning and support points remain comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C replaces uniformly reported 10,000-iteration runs with longer, sample-size-dependent mixture runs and 100,000-iteration OpenML runs. It also changes the mixture configuration from noise injection and zero initialization to no additional noise and initialization near zero. KT uses centered kernels, g=6 and revised candidate handling. However, v2 Section 5 retains conflicting noise and iteration descriptions, leaving the executed settings partly ambiguous.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 investigates two important comparison issues: centered versus uncentered KT across all three retained datasets (Figure 7), and oversampling sensitivity for g=0,2,4,6 (Figure 6). These substantially extend the existing stationarity, noise-condition and Matérn-kernel analyses.

E5.justification: The main comparison retains averages over 20 independent seeds and 25%–75% quantile shading. New Table 1 adds plus/minus uncertainty summaries without defining their meaning or specifying a table-specific run count. This changes reporting without establishing additional repetitions or a new estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Benchmark curves are revised, particularly KT results in the main comparison and Figure 5, substantially narrowing its displayed disadvantage under changed settings. v2 adds Table 1, Figures 6–7 and a runtime comparison of approximately 20 seconds versus over 3,000 seconds for KT at n=100. The reported convergence slopes −1.39 and −1.35 remain unchanged. These are not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Lemma B.8 and Theorem 4.1 change the concentration factor from beta_t to sqrt(gamma beta_t), with a substantially rewritten Appendix B.4.2 proof. Corollary 4.2 expands its stated horizon from n^(1/(2 alpha)) to n^(1/alpha). New Corollary B.10 and Remark 4.5 add guarantees conditional on good initialization. The Section 3 super-convergence statements remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The two central claims—faster-than-MMD integration error and computability through finite-particle gradient flow—remain. The introduction now explicitly exempts kernel thinning from the claimed theory–practice gap, while the conclusion adds applicability to large-scale deep-learning coreset construction.

C2.justification: v2 explains the earlier KT comparison's unfairness and discusses the revised cost–accuracy trade-off. It adds a good-initialization interpretation and qualifies Assumption 5 verification as excluding initial iterations. Conversely, it removes explicit limitations concerning numerical approximation of kernel expectations, general-manifold extensions and the open SVGD super-convergence question.

D1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands reproducibility information: specific Goodpoints functions, KT failure probability and swap settings, candidate-pool construction, support-point iteration budgets and a step-size search grid. These include newly disclosed details rather than demonstrated changes to every implementation. The stated code-repository pointer also changes from MMDF_cubature to stationary_mmd.

R1.justification: v2 refines positioning around kernel thinning by acknowledging its guarantees and discussing generalized, debiased and low-rank variants. It adds corresponding citations and removes the SVGD moment-matching and rate-doubling discussions and references. Most existing related-work coverage and the central stationary-versus-minimum distinction remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introductory wording are edited, with widespread replacement of 'cubature' by 'numerical integration.' Sections 3–4 lose subsection divisions, the discussion is shortened and Appendix C gains subsections, while the overall exposition remains recognizable. v2 also introduces unresolved B.5/B.6 references and incorrectly labels many referenced propositions or lemmas as theorems.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and two substantial multipanel figures, Figures 6–7. The exactness plot moves from a main-text inset to Appendix C, becoming Figure 3; the main comparison becomes Figure 2 with a revised legend. Main-text equations are also compressed and reflowed, materially changing the presentation of the evidence.

improvement.justification: The revised KT comparison addresses a meaningful fairness problem, and the new sensitivity studies and implementation details strengthen empirical assessment. However, Appendix C contradicts Section 5 on experimental settings, explicit limitations disappear, and Corollary 4.2's proof still substitutes beta_t for the newly introduced sqrt(gamma beta_t) factor. These unresolved empirical and theoretical inconsistencies prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
